USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

rockwood — pattern 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A cyclist has AC joint pain after a fall. The AC ligaments are disrupted, but the coracoclavicular ligaments are sprained rather than completely torn. Imaging shows mild AC displacement with only a small increase in coracoclavicular distance. Which Rockwood acromioclavicular injury type best fits this pattern?

  1. Type V
  2. Type VI
  3. Type II
  4. Type III
  5. Type IV
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Type II

Type II: AC ligament disruption with coracoclavicular ligament sprain and mild displacement.

Understanding the options

Type II
Type II: AC ligament disruption with coracoclavicular ligament sprain and mild displacement.
Type III
Type III describes complete AC and CC ligament disruption with superior displacement and a coracoclavicular distance increase of about 25–100%. The case instead matches Type II.
Type IV
Type IV describes posterior displacement of the distal clavicle into or through the trapezius. The case instead matches Type II.
Type V
Type V describes marked superior displacement with extensive deltotrapezial disruption and a coracoclavicular distance increase greater than 100%. The case instead matches Type II.
Type VI
Type VI describes inferior displacement of the distal clavicle, beneath the acromion or coracoid. The case instead matches Type II.
